card.name: Linking words before cause-attribution phrases
card.fires_on: Small linking words (could, is, to, factors, possible) in label sentences about whether a drug caused an event, just before words like cause, etiology, excluded or unknown.

modes.label: Causality cannot be excluded
modes.description: A helper word after a drug's contribution to an adverse event, ahead of a statement that the role is unknown or not ruled out.
modes.example: The contribution of bosentan in these cases<< could>> not be excluded.

modes.label: No other cause found
modes.description: The word "is" after "no other etiology" in advice to stop a drug.
modes.example: Consider discontinuation of olmesartan medoxomil in cases where no other etiology<< is>> found (5.5) .

modes.label: Possible cause wording
modes.description: A word leading into cause or confounder language.
modes.example: Consider the drug as a<< possible>> cause for severe joint pain and discontinue

card.writes: It pushes toward cause-related continuations and away from blame or attribution words.
card.plain: It marks spots in a label where the text is about to say whether the drug is the cause of a problem.
